rationale: The candidate reads as a single compact block with one notch-like subtraction, so it has some repair integrity and a weak dominant gesture, but it does not yet form a convincing neighborhood-living mass. Across the four views the form remains mostly box-like, with only a small semantic response at the access edge and no clearly public court, terrace, or active ground threshold. The top view shows a plain rectangle inside the parcel rather than a parcel-responsive open-space figure; the blue frontage edge is not answered by a legible void or entry seam. The overall section is flat and generic, closer to a sealed extrusion than a compact capacity-aware street building. It therefore fails program_fit_hard_pass because the visible mass does not yet support the required active ground edge and public void logic, even though it is coherent and not badly clipped.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More pavilion/cultural than compact neighborhood living; the bridge-and-courtyard language is useful but the overall object is more open and sculptural than this candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Carved central void with a clear mass/void hierarchy and a calm upper cap can support a neighborhood program if the ground edge stays active.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger campus-like condition; do not copy the scale or tower perimeter, only the courtyard hierarchy.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A courtyard-plaza composition with stepped/terraced blocks can organize multiple masses while preserving a public center.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is more civic/retail and facade-driven; the candidate should keep massing logic, not surface articulation.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A shallow recessed void or cutout at the frontage can make a box legible as a public building without over-fragmenting it.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is too compact to adopt the broad horizontal spread; use the void/roof relationship only.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: An elongated mass with a central atrium and folded roof can create a clear program core and active public interior threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is more spread-out and landscape-oriented; candidate needs a simpler, more compact version of the same sectional hierarchy.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced wings around a core and a connecting bridge produce a strong neighborhood figure with a readable public center.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied visually, but the mass underuses the parcel and does not organize the site around a public open-space figure.
Access edge response is weak: the verified frontage is not met by a clearly legible court, undercut, or entry seam.
The form is coherent in all views but too generic; it risks reading as a simple box with a minor notch rather than a neighborhood building.

No structural graph edits are proposed because the snapshot exposes only the protected notch controller and no editable nodes beyond it; the current massing should be re-authored upstream if a stronger courtyard or split-wing response is needed.
